# Setting Up
```{r}
#| label: Set-Up
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Load in dataset

library("here")
library("tidyverse")
library("tidytuesdayR")

if (!dir.exists(here("data"))) {
    dir.create(here("data"))
}

b_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
ts_lyrics <- readRDS(here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
sales <- readRDS(here("data", "sales.RDS"))

rds_files <- c("b_lyrics.RDS", "ts_lyrics.RDS", "sales.RDS")
## Check whether we have all 3 files
if (any(!file.exists(here("data", rds_files)))) {
    ## If we don't, then download the data
    b_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/beyonce_lyrics.csv")
    ts_lyrics <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/taylor_swift_lyrics.csv")
    sales <- readr::read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/master/data/2020/2020-09-29/sales.csv")

    ## Then save the data objects to RDS files
    saveRDS(b_lyrics, file = here("data", "b_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(ts_lyrics, file = here("data", "ts_lyrics.RDS"))
    saveRDS(sales, file = here("data", "sales.RDS"))
}
```

# Part 1: Explore Album Sales 
## Part 1A: 
```{r}
#| label: Part 1A
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

glimpse(sales)

sales_tidy <- sales |>
    ## Removes "extra stuff" from datesm then convert use stringr to get date (includes regular expression)
    mutate(
        released = str_remove(released, " \\([A-Z]+\\)\\[[0-9]+\\]"),
        released = mdy(released)
    ) |>
    ## Use forcats to create a factor called country 
    mutate(country = fct_collapse(country,
        "World" = c("World", "WW"),
        "FRA"   = c("FRA", "FR")
    )) |>
    ## Convert sales to album sales in millions of dollars.
    mutate(sales = sales / 1000000) |>
    ## Keep only album sales from the UK, the US or the World
    filter(country %in% c("UK", "US", "World"))

## Auto print your final wrangled tibble data frame.
sales_tidy



```

## Part 1B: 
```{r}
#| label: Part 1B
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

sales_us <- sales_tidy |>
    ## Keep only US states
    filter(country == "US") |>
    ## Get release years and go to whole number (source below)
    mutate(
        years_since_release = floor(interval(released, today()) / years(1))
    )

sales_us

## Group by Artist, summarizing by most recent, oldest, and median years since release by artist
sales_us |>
    group_by(artist) |>
    summarize(
        most_recent = min(years_since_release),
        oldest      = max(years_since_release),
        median      = median(years_since_release)
    )
```

Sources I used to help me complete this: 

https://lubridate.tidyverse.org/reference/interval.html

https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/Round

## Part 1C 
```{r}
#| label: Part 1C
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Get total album sales in millions by artist and country using Part 1A data
total_sales <- sales_tidy |>
    group_by(artist, country) |>
    ## Added .groups = drops from error in console 
    summarize(total_sales = sum(sales), .groups = "drop")
total_sales

##  Creating a percent stacked bar chart
total_sales |>
    ## Setting aes with x and y respectively, incorporating info for stacked bar chart 
    ggplot(aes(x = artist, y = total_sales, fill = country)) +
    geom_bar(position = "fill", stat = "identity") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    ## Settinf labels 
    labs(
        title = "Studio album sales by country",
        subtitle = "Beyoncé vs. Taylor Swift (UK, US, and World)",
        x = "Artist",
        y = "Percentage of total album sales (millions)",
        fill = "Country"
    )
```

Sources I used to help me complete this: 

https://r-graph-gallery.com/48-grouped-barplot-with-ggplot2

https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/scale_continuous.html

## Part 1E
```{r}
#| label: Part 1E
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Data from Part 1A
sales_tidy |>
    ## Setting x, y, and color
    ggplot(aes(x = released, y = sales, color = artist)) +
    ## Setting point size
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    ## Using facet by rows (stacked)
    facet_grid(country ~ .) +
    scale_x_date(date_breaks = "1 year", date_labels = "%Y")+ 
    ## Setting labels

        title = "Studio album sales by release date",
        x = "Release date",
        y = "Album sales (millions)",
        color = "Artist"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
        )
```

# Part 2: Exploring sentiment of lyrics
## Part 2A
```{r}
#| label: Part 2A
#| warning: false
#| echo: true
library("tidytext")

## One row per lyric line (keeps Album, Title, etc.)
ts_lines <- ts_lyrics %>%
    unnest_tokens(
        output = line,
        input = Lyrics,
        token = "lines",
        ## Keeping original capitalization for display purposes 
        to_lower = FALSE 
    )

## Filtering for "hello"
ts_hello <- ts_lines %>%
    filter(str_detect(line, regex("hello", ignore_case = TRUE)))

## Getting nrow of hellow 
ts_hello %>% print(n = Inf)
nrow(ts_hello)

## Filtering for goodbye "goodbye"
ts_goodbye <- ts_lines %>%
    filter(str_detect(line, regex("goodbye", ignore_case = TRUE)))

## Getting nrow of goodbye 
ts_goodbye %>% print(n = Inf)
nrow(ts_goodbye)

## Print line 
cat("There are", nrow(ts_hello), "lines with \"hello\" and", nrow(ts_goodbye), "lines with \"goodbye\" in ts_lyrics.")
```

## Part 2C
```{r}
#| label: Part 2C
#| warning: false
#| echo: true
library(wordcloud)
?wordcloud

## Completing numbers 1-7
b_top25 <- b_lyrics %>%
    ## 1. One word per row 
    unnest_tokens(output = word, input = line, token = "words") %>% 
    ## 2. Removing stop words 
    anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") %>%                           
    ## 3. Calculate the total number for each word in the lyrics
    count(word) %>%                                                   # 3. total per word (column n)
    ## 4. Add column with Bing sentiment 
    inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"), by = "word") %>%               # 4. add bing sentiment
    ## 5. Sort the rows from most frequent to least frequent words
    arrange(desc(n)) %>%                                             
    ## 6. Top 25 most frequent words
    slice_head(n = 25)                                                

## 7. Auto print the wrangled tibble data frame
b_top25                                                              

## Creating the bar plot
b_top25 %>%
    mutate(word = fct_reorder(word, n)) %>%
    ## GGplot using aes setting x and y respectively 
    ggplot(aes(x = n, y = word, fill = sentiment)) +
    geom_col() +
    ## Source for this below ; I decided to add so we can see exact values since x range is so vast 
    geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 2) +
    ## Setting labels 
    labs(
        title = "Top 25 sentiment words in Beyoncé's lyrics",
        subtitle = "Stopwords removed (sentiment from the bing lexicon)",
        x = "Frequency (number of times the word appears)",
        y = "Word",
        fill = "Bing sentiment"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

# Step 9: word cloud
set.seed(1000)
## Source for Random Order below 
b_top25 %>%
    with(wordcloud(word, n, max.words = 25, random.order = FALSE))

```

## Part 2D
```{r}
#| label: Part 2D
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Completing numbers 1-7
ts_top25 <- ts_lines %>%
    ## 1. One word per row (ts_lines from Part 2A has one lyric line per row)
    unnest_tokens(output = word, input = line, token = "words") %>%
    ## 2. Removing stop words
    anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") %>%
    ## 3. Calculate the total number for each word in the lyrics
    count(word) %>%
    ## 4. Add column with Bing sentiment
    inner_join(get_sentiments("bing"), by = "word") %>%
    ## 5. Sort the rows from most frequent to least frequent words
    arrange(desc(n)) %>%
    ## 6. Top 25 most frequent words
    slice_head(n = 25)

## 7. Auto print the wrangled tibble data frame
ts_top25

## Creating the bar plot
ts_top25 %>%
    mutate(word = fct_reorder(word, n)) %>%
    ## ggplot using aes setting x and y respectively
    ggplot(aes(x = n, y = word, fill = sentiment)) +
    geom_col() +
    ## Adding counts at the end of each bar (geom_text, ggplot2 documentation)
    geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 2) +
    ## Extra space on the right so the longest bar's label isn't cut off
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
    ## Setting labels
    labs(
        title = "Top 25 sentiment words in Taylor Swift's lyrics",
        subtitle = "Stopwords removed (sentiment from the bing lexicon)",
        x = "Frequency (number of times the word appears)",
        y = "Word",
        fill = "Bing sentiment"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()+
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

## Word cloud of the top 25 words
set.seed(1000)
ts_top25 %>%
    with(wordcloud(word, n, max.words = 25, random.order = FALSE))
```

Sources I used to help me complete this are same for Part 2C.
## Part 2E
```{r}
#| label: Part 2E
#| warning: false
#| echo: true

## Ran tidytext::get_sentiments("afinn") in console 

## Completing Parts 1-6 
ts_album_sentiment <- ts_lyrics %>%
    ## Clean album names (remove white space at end) so they match the sales data (source below)
    mutate(Album = str_to_title(str_trim(Album))) %>%
    ## 1. One word per row
    unnest_tokens(output = word, input = Lyrics, token = "words") %>%
    ## 2. Removing stop words
    anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") %>%
    ## 3. Calculate the total number for each word in the lyrics for each Album
    count(Album, word) %>%
    ## 4. Add column with afinn sentiment score 
    inner_join(get_sentiments("afinn"), by = "word") %>%
    ## 5. Calculate the average sentiment score for each album, weighted by how often each word appears
    group_by(Album) %>%
    summarize(avg_sentiment = sum(value * n) / sum(n))

## 6. Auto print
ts_album_sentiment

## 7. Join with Part 1A US sales
ts_sentiment_sales <- sales_tidy %>%
    filter(artist == "Taylor Swift", country == "US") %>%
    inner_join(ts_album_sentiment, by = c("title" = "Album"))

ts_sentiment_sales

## 8-10. Scatter plot
ts_sentiment_sales %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = released, y = avg_sentiment)) +
    geom_point(aes(size = sales), color = "hotpink") +
    ## 9. Horizontal line at 0 (neutral sentiment) SOurce below 
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid") +
    ## Album names above each point (source same as above parts)
    geom_text(aes(label = title), vjust = -1.5, size = 3) +
    ## Adding labels to the graph 
    labs(
        title = "Sentiment of Taylor Swift's albums over time",
        subtitle = "Average afinn sentiment score per album (stopwords removed)",
        caption = "Point size = US sales",
        x = "Album release date",
        y = "Average sentiment score (afinn scale, -5 to 5)",
        size = "US sales (in millions)"
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))

```

Sources I used to help me complete this: 
https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/ggplot2/versions/0.9.1/topics/geom_hline

https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/stringr/versions/1.6.0/topics/str_trim

10. Taylor Swift's albums have decreased in sentiment over time. Her first two albums (Taylor Swift and Fearless) have the highest average sentiment scores. The albums following that have had a relatively neutral sentiment score, except for 1989 which is negative. One could argue that Red has a slightly higher score, but it is still only around 0.25 on the graph. We can also see how sentiment does not necessarily track sales. 1989, having the lowest sentiment score was one of her best-selling albums, as was Fearless which had one of the highest scores.
